Name: Consumer Price Index
Description: Headline CPI measuring consumer price inflation.
Why Useful: Core measure for identifying inflation regimes.

Name: Core CPI
Why Useful: Shows underlying inflation pressure without volatile components.

Name: Producer Price Index
Why Useful: Can show upstream inflation pressure before it reaches consumers.

Name: 10Y Breakeven Inflation
Why Useful: Shows whether inflation expectations are becoming unanchored.

Name: 5Y Breakeven Inflation
Why Useful: Captures shorter-term inflation expectation pressure.

Name: Michigan Inflation Expectations
Why Useful: Useful for comparing consumer expectations against market expectations.

Name: Effective Federal Funds Rate
Description: Policy rate targeted by the Federal Reserve.
Why Useful: Shows monetary policy stance across regimes.

Name: 2-Year Treasury Yield
Why Useful: Sensitive to expected Fed policy.

Name: 10-Year Treasury Yield
Why Useful: Reflects growth, inflation expectations, and term premium.

Name: 10-Year Real Yield
Why Useful: Shows real discount-rate pressure after inflation adjustment.

Name: 30-Year Mortgage Rate
Why Useful: Shows how tightening transmits into housing affordability.

Name: 10Y-2Y Treasury Spread
Why Useful: Classic recession leading indicator through curve inversion.

Name: 10Y-3M Treasury Spread
Why Useful: Another widely used yield-curve recession signal.

Name: M2 Money Supply
Why Useful: Tracks liquidity conditions and monetary expansion/contraction.

Name: Monetary Base
Description: Currency in circulation plus reserve balances.
Why Useful: Shows central-bank balance sheet/liquidity expansion.

Name: Unemployment Rate
Why Useful: Captures labor-market deterioration and recession severity.

Name: Nonfarm Payrolls
Why Useful: Tracks employment growth and labor-market momentum.

Name: Average Hourly Earnings
Description: Average hourly earnings of production/nonsupervisory workers.
Why Useful: Useful proxy for wage pressure and sticky inflation.

Name: Job Openings
Description: Number of job openings from JOLTS.
Why Useful: Measures labor demand and tightness.

Name: WTI Crude Oil Price
Description: Daily West Texas Intermediate crude oil price.
Why Useful: Captures commodity shocks that can feed inflation.

Name: Gold Volatility Index
Why Useful: Captures uncertainty and safe-haven volatility.

Name: Case-Shiller Home Price Index
Why Useful: Tracks housing-market strength and rate-sensitive stress.

Name: Trade-Weighted U.S. Dollar
Description: Broad nominal trade-weighted U.S. dollar index.
Why Useful: Shows dollar strength, imported inflation pressure, and flight-to-safety behavior.

Name: NBER Recession Indicator
Description: Binary recession indicator based on NBER recession dates.
Why Useful: Used to shade official recession periods.

Name: Smoothed Recession Probability
Why Useful: Useful for comparing market/macro signals against recession risk.
